title: Le, la, un, une…
intro: In French every noun is **masculine** or **feminine**, and the little word in front of it — the **article** — shows which. This lesson covers all of them: *le, la, l', les* (the) and *un, une, des* (a, some).

cases.label: masculine or feminine?
cases.rule: For people, the gender usually follows the person: *le père, la mère*. For everything else, learn the article with the noun. *le bébé* is always masculine.

cases.label: le — the (masculine)
cases.rule: **le** + a masculine noun: *le père, le frère*.

cases.label: la — the (feminine)
cases.rule: **la** + a feminine noun: *la mère, la sœur*.

cases.label: l' — before a vowel
cases.rule: **le** and **la** become **l'** before a vowel or a silent **h**: *l'oncle, l'enfant, l'homme*.

cases.label: les — the (plural)
cases.rule: **les** for every plural, masculine or feminine. Before a vowel you hear a /z/: *les‿enfants*.

cases.label: un — a (masculine)
cases.rule: **un** + a masculine noun: *un frère*. Before a vowel you hear an /n/: *un‿enfant*.

cases.label: une — a (feminine)
cases.rule: **une** + a feminine noun: *une sœur*. **une** never shortens: *une amie*.

cases.label: des — some (plural)
cases.rule: **des** is the plural of *un / une*. English often says nothing: *J'ai des cousins* = I have cousins.

cases.label: plural: a silent -s
cases.rule: Add **-s** for the plural, but don't say it: *frère* and *frères* sound the same. You hear the plural in the article: *le* /lə/ → *les* /le/. Words ending in **-s** don't change: *les fils*.

cases.label: le or un?
cases.rule: **le / la / les**: the one we both know, or things in general (*J'aime les enfants*). **un / une / des**: one, some, not a specific one (*C'est un ami*).

sections.title: 1. Masculine or feminine?
text: Every French noun has a gender. For people it's easy: it usually follows the person.
For things, there is often no logic, so **always learn a noun with its article**: not *famille* but **la famille**.

examples.en: The baby is small. (bébé is always masculine)

sections.tip: In this app, masculine words are **blue** and feminine words are **pink**.

sections.title: 2. The: le, la, l', les

head: the
Example
rows: before a vowel or silent h

sections.tip: Listen: **le** /lə/ and **les** /le/ sound different — often that is the only way to hear a plural.

sections.title: 3. A, an, some: un, une, des
sections.tip: Before a vowel you hear a link: *un‿enfant* /œ̃.nɑ̃.fɑ̃/, *des‿enfants* /de.zɑ̃.fɑ̃/.

sections.title: 4. One or more: the plural
text: Most nouns add **-s** in the plural. The -s is silent, so *frère* and *frères* sound exactly the same — listen to the article instead.
Nouns that already end in **-s** don't change: *le fils → les fils*.

sections.title: 5. le or un?
text: **un / une / des**: one or some — not a specific one, or something new: *C'est un ami*.
**le / la / les**: the one we both know: *Le frère de Léa s'appelle Hugo*. Also for things in general, especially after **aimer**: *J'aime les enfants*.

mistakes.why: French needs an article. For “some”, use **des**.
A woman friend is **une amie**; a man is **un ami**.

story.title: La photo
story.en: Tom looks at a photo of Léa's family.

lines.en: Oh, a photo! Is that your family?

lines.fr: Oui ! C'est {la famille|art-la} de mon père.

lines.en: And the man there, who's that?

lines.fr: C'est {le père|art-le} de mon père : mon grand-père Jacques.
lines.en: That's my father's father: my grandfather Jacques.
And the woman with the baby?

lines.fr: C'est ma mère, avec Lou, ma petite sœur. Lou, c'est {une fille|art-une}, mais on dit « {le bébé|art-gender} » !
lines.en: That's my mother, with Lou, my little sister. Lou is a girl, but we say “le bébé”!

lines.fr: Et {les enfants|art-les}, là ? Ce sont {des cousins|art-des} ?
lines.en: And the children there? Are they cousins?

lines.fr: Oui. Ce sont {les enfants|art-les} de {l'oncle|art-l} Pierre : Jules et Chloé.
lines.en: Yes. They're uncle Pierre's children: Jules and Chloé.

lines.fr: Oui ! Et moi, j'ai {un cousin|art-un} à Montréal aussi.
lines.en: Yes! And I have a cousin in Montreal too.
I have a brother and two sisters.

lines.fr: Moi aussi ! C'est {une famille|art-which} très sympa.
lines.en: Me too! It's a really nice family.

quiz.why: **bébé** is always masculine, even for a girl.

quiz.q: ___ tante de Tom habite à Londres.

quiz.en: She's a friend of my mother's.

quiz.why: No word in English, but French needs **des**.

quiz.en: My two sisters are in Paris.

quiz.why: **fils** already ends in **-s**, so the plural doesn't change.
